messages.subject: Can I obtain first chain of the posterior samples if the program stopped before the second chain?
parts:
Dear Mailing users,
I am starting to use Rstan only recently. I have run 4 chains sampling in my laptop, after 4 days, it finish the first chain of sampling, but it showed up a error message " cannot allocate vector of size 8kb". I still want to have the results of the first chain, is there a way to get the first chain samples ? How would I know how much memeory I need if I need to run 4 chains ?
Attached my script in the email.
thank you, Irene

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Can I obtain first chain of the posterior samples if the program stopped before the second chain?
parts:
You should have the samples.csv file if you ran through
the command line, but if you're running through R, I don't think
there's a way to recover the data.

We've been suggesting for users that they run fewer iterations
first to make sure the model works and to get a look at output.
There's no way to debug if things go wrong after a 4-day run.

If you were using multivariate models, the problem
you may have been having is a memory leak we patched
for the 1.2 release which is due out any second now.
One reason it might've taken a long time is if your computer
went to swapping memory out for virtual memory on file.

- Bob

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: Can I obtain first chain of the posterior samples if the program stopped before the second chain?
parts:
On Wednesday, March 6, 2013 5:04:48 PM UTC-5, Irene Zeng wrote:
Dear Mailing users,
I am starting to use Rstan only recently. I have run 4 chains sampling in my laptop, after 4 days, it finish the first chain of sampling, but it showed up a error message " cannot allocate vector of size 8kb". I still want to have the results of the first chain, is there a way to get the first chain samples ? How would I know how much memeory I need if I need to run 4 chains ?

There is an option for stan() called sample_file that can be passed a character string to write the samples to a file. In addition, it is possible to call stan() in parallel using any of the parallel frameworks that R supports. The main problem with memory in your model is that you define mu as a transformed parameter that has length 78400! Even if you wrote the samples to a disk, you could easily crash R when you loaded them into RAM. I personally would define mu as a local vector in the model section so that its samples are used but not stored. In addition, it is wasteful to embark on a 4 day run without optimizing your code. The main areas where your code would go faster are using matrix algebra rather than scalar algebra, using the vectorized forms of the distributions rather than manually looping over all the observations, and using bernoulli_logit() instead of bernoulli(inv_logit(...)).

Ben

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: Can I obtain first chain of the posterior samples if the program stopped before the second chain?
parts:
multi_normal requires a vector for the variate and location
arguments (vector). You're giving it arrays (real[1]).

So you must have something declared as

real g[N];

which should be declared as

vector[N] g;

- Bob

>      >         have the results of the first chain, is there a way to get the first chain samples ? How would I know how
>     much
>      >         memeory I need if I need to run 4 chains ?
>      >
>      >
>      >     There is an option for stan() called sample_file that can be passed a character string to write the samples to a
>      >     file. In addition, it is possible to call stan() in parallel using any of the parallel frameworks that R
>     supports.
>      >     The main problem with memory in your model is that you define mu as a transformed parameter that has length
>     78400!
>      >     Even if you wrote the samples to a disk, you could easily crash R when you loaded them into RAM. I personally
>     would
>      >     define mu as a local vector in the model section so that its samples are used but not stored. In addition, it is
>      >     wasteful to embark on a 4 day run without optimizing your code. The main areas where your code would go
>     faster are
>      >     using matrix algebra rather than scalar algebra, using the vectorized forms of the distributions rather than
>      >     manually looping over all the observations, and using bernoulli_logit() instead of bernoulli(inv_logit(...)).
>      >

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: Can I obtain first chain of the posterior samples if the program stopped before the second chain?
parts:
On 3/8/13 10:02 AM, Ben Goodrich wrote:
> On Friday, March 8, 2013 4:23:17 AM UTC-5, Irene wrote:
>
> thanks, you are right. I change the declaration for g and mn as vector[] , the message gone. Now I also want to sample
> the row vector of the matrix U[200,3] from multi_normal distribution, I have tried several version. this is the last
> one,
> but not work..Irene
>
>
> I don't think multi_normal is defined for row vectors. Only column vectors and matrices.

Correct. You can find a convenient list of all the
signatures for all the functions supported by Stan in
the index.

So what you need to do is apply a transpose. So if x
is the column vector, instead of writing "x ~ multi_normal(...)"
write "x' ~ multi_normal(...)". Same for the location vector,
which also has to be a vector.

We'll probably generalize the multivariate normal when
we get around to vectorizing it.

- Bob
